title: A basic Express server
idea: An Express server is a Node process that listens on a port and answers each request with the first route that matches.
points: A route pairs a method and path with a handler.
`app.listen` opens the port. Without it, the process registers routes and exits.
Read the port from `process.env.PORT`; environment values are always strings.
A request that matches no route gets Express's built-in 404 reply.

items.label: Load the env
items.text: dotenv copies `.env` values into `process.env`, so `PORT` is available.

items.label: Create the app
items.text: `express()` returns an app that will hold your routes and middleware.

items.label: Register a route
items.text: `app.get('/', handler)` records the route. The handler does not run yet.

items.label: Listen
items.text: `app.listen(port)` opens the port. Node stays alive, waiting for requests.

items.label: Handle a request
items.text: `GET /` matches the route, so the handler runs and sends the reply.

code.title: src/index.js
code.caption: Save as `src/index.js`. This copy calls itself once, then closes; in the project, `.env` sets `PORT`.

walk.text: Import Express and create the app.
Read the port from the environment. Here `0` asks the system for any free port.
Register one route. It sends plain text.
`listen` opens the port. `err` is set if that failed, so throw it.
Call the route and print the status and body.
An unknown path gets the built-in 404.
Close the server so the script can exit.

pitfalls: Forget `listen` and the script ends silently: nothing serves requests.
A busy port gives `EADDRINUSE` in the `listen` callback; throw `err` to see it.
Keep `process.env.PORT` out of arithmetic until you wrap it in `Number()`.

quiz.why: Environment values are strings, so `+` joins the text. Use `Number(process.env.PORT)` for arithmetic.

takeaway: Routes describe replies; `listen` is what opens the port.
